title: Backup file_logger should store relative paths
description_shown:
h2. Summary

Backup {{file_logger}} should serialize a relative path (just the filename) rather than the absolute {{$CFG->backuptempdir/$backupid.log}}. 

The absolute path is host specific and ends up baked into the backup controller record and into the {{.mbz}} artefact, which makes backups non portable and causes restore code to blindly open whatever path was deserialized. Storing a relative path and rebuilding the full path on the fly using the current {{$CFG->backuptempdir}} fixes both.

h2. Background

This came out of [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-76288|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-76288|smart-link], which fixed {{backup_cleanup_task}} crashing when {{$CFG->backuptempdir}} had changed since the controller was serialised. {{file_logger::__wakeup}} now needs to also handle relative paths, this ticket adds that read-side support alongside switching the writer to produce relative paths.

title: Fix bug in lib/lti1p3 causing omitted line item properties to be sent as nulls during deep linking return
description_shown:
This is one of two blockers to using the new certification tooling at build.1edtech to certify (or re-certify) our LTI Provider as LTI Advantage Complete. Right now, during a deep linking workflow, after content selection (and assuming “add to gradebook” IS checked), the cert. suite reports:

{noformat}"errors": [
    "'label' should be a string",
    "'tag' should be a string"
],{noformat}

Moodle doesn’t set label or tag on the lineitem when returning it as part of the content item, however. See the code responsible for that response here:
[https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/f747c15cbf1c1c963a9592a73b167b969ec33d75/public/enrol/lti/configure.php#L76|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/f747c15cbf1c1c963a9592a73b167b969ec33d75/public/enrol/lti/configure.php#L76|smart-link] 

What should happen is that, because we’ve omitted those fields (i.e. we’re not calling setLabel() or setTag()), the label and tag properties should be excluded from the contentitem’s lineitem. These fields are optional per the spec: [https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-dl/v2p0#lti-resource-link|https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-dl/v2p0#lti-resource-link|smart-link]  

If these fields are omitted, the certification suite’s diagnosis window reports everything is green and passing.

title: Generate development and production outputs for ESM code
description_shown:
Initially we went with a single build for the ESM outputs. In [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88786|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88786|smart-link] we simplified this build because it was generating different output depending on whether the build was run in watch mode or not - the watch would generate a ‘dev' build with some different options for minify, sourcemapping, etc.

Now we know we do not want a different built depending on how the code is built, but this did later raise the question of whether we wanted a dev build at all.

In our YUI days we generated three outputs:

* min.js - a minified version for production
* .js - a non-minified version for …????
* -debug.js - a non-minified version with debugging

We did away with this with AMD.

And now I feel like we should come back to it with our new React overlord as it has a number of benefits when it comes to React client-side tooling and management.

The advantages as I see it:

* React profiler can be enabled/disabled based on the version used
* Source maps can be provided to clients for Development only
* Various other development features can be enabled for development, including:
** jsxDev
** keepNames
** minify



Whilst an improvement we shoudl still backport this change, which is in keeping with the policy we have for AMD changes. I don’t anticipate many people using ESM in 5.2, but it is still supported.

title: Routing: Handle behaviour for restricted sections
description_shown:
The linear course navigation must correctly handle *Sections* that are hidden or restricted based on access rules. We need to ensure that the 'Next' and 'Previous' routes lead students to the expected pages, specifically respecting the restricted section implementation (and the corresponding landing pages for restricted content).

h3. 🎯 Required action

* Ensure that sections marked as ‘Hidden’ from students (restricted with eye closed or hidden) are entirely skipped in the linear sequence, including all activities within them.
* Confirm that sections that are restricted but visible to students (eye open) are included in the linear sequence. 'Next' should lead to the section landing page where restriction requirements are displayed.
* The navigation sequence must update dynamically as a student unlocks a previously restricted section.

h3. (/) Acceptance criteria

* Students must not see a ‘Next’ or ‘Previous’ route pointing to a section (or its contents) that is fully hidden from their view.
* If a section is visible but restricted (locked), going to ‘Next’ from the previous activity must navigate the user to that section's landing page to show why it is locked.
* Verify that teachers/admins can still navigate through all sections (regardless of hide/restrict settings) to preview the full course flow.

title: Convert Entity Custom Field Category to Shared Category
description_shown:
Add functionality to allow converting an existing entity-specific custom field (CF) category into a shared custom field category.

* A regular entity CF category (e.g. Course, Cohort, etc.) can be converted into a shared category.
* The conversion will be triggered directly from the category actions on the Entity Custom Fields page. The user who triggers the conversion needs to be able to configure custom fields in both entities (origin and shared).
* Before completing the conversion, display a confirmation modal informing the user that this action is irreversible.
* Once converted, the category will be enabled for the source entity by default. This will be stated in the confirmation modal.
* All existing custom field values stored for this category across entities must remain intact and continue to function after the conversion.
* After the conversion, a toast should be displayed with a confirmation message.
* If a shared custom field category with the same name already exists, the conversion should still proceed without errors.
* If any custom field within the category being converted has a short name that already exists in a shared custom field category, the conversion must be blocked. In this case, display a notice to the user explaining why the conversion cannot proceed. The notice should advise the user to update the conflicting custom field short name before retrying the conversion.

title: Performance regression after implementing MDL-60912

title: Single quotes in search query return no results on MSSQL (non full-text fallback path)
description_shown:
h3. Summary

When using the Simple search engine ({{search_simpledb}}) on a site where {{is_fulltext_search_supported()}} returns false (e.g. MSSQL without full-text search installed), searching for a term containing a single quote (e.g. it's) returns no results.

!Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 18-37-50 Global search int_nftss.png|width=250!

Single quotes

!Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 18-38-04 Global search int_nftss.png|width=250!

Double quotes

h3. Root Cause

In {{search/engine/simpledb/classes/engine.php}}, the {{get_simple_query()}} method only strips double quotes from the query string before building the LIKE-based SQL:

{noformat}$q = str_replace('"', '', $q);{noformat}

Single quotes are left untouched, which causes the LIKE '%it's%' parameter to effectively break on MSSQL, silently returning no results.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Set up a Moodle site on MSSQL without full-text search enabled
# Enable global search with Simple search engine
# Index some content
# Search for a term containing a single quote (e.g. it's or Moodle's)
# Observe: no results returned

h3. Expected Behaviour

Search results containing the term should be returned, with the single quote either stripped or properly handled.

h3. Suggested Fix

In get_simple_query(), also strip single quotes:

{noformat}> $q = str_replace(['"', "'"], '', $q);{noformat}

title: Add Moodle 5.2.0 upgrade line to all the upgrade.php scripts
description_shown:
To have it properly detected for the future, it would be great to add to all the upgrade.php scripts some lines like these:

{code:php}// Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade line.
// Put any upgrade step following this.{code}

exactly before the "{{return true;}}" present in all the scripts.

Normally, it's ok to do that both in the stable (502_STABLE) and the {{main}} branches, so they will allow quickly find where 5.2.0 started and act once we decide future requirements.

But, *when under parallel development, this only can be done in the stable (502_STABLE) branch* as the {{main}} branch already has diverged and can have own upgrade steps not corresponding to the version just released, but to the future version being developed in parallel.

The change can be performed globally with:

{code:java}#!/bin/bash
export rel="5.2.0" && find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | \
grep '/db/' | \
xargs grep -L "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
xargs perl -p -i -e 's@( *)(return true;)@\1// Automatically generated Moodle v$ENV{rel} release upgrade line.\n\1// Put any upgrade step following this.\n\n\1\2@s'{code}

{code:java}find . -name upgrade.php | xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | grep '/db/' | xargs grep -L 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade'{code}

title: TypeError when trying to use \core\route\require_login for courseless login checks
description_shown:
I’m trying to implement a controller for a non-course-centric route, using the following attribute helper:

{noformat}...
requirelogin: new require_login(
    requirelogin: true,
    autologinguest: false,
)
...{noformat}

This is synonymous with the old require_login(null, false); login is required, but not for a course.

Currently, the above results in a TypeError because moodle_authentication_middleware calls $requirements->get_course_attribute_name(), which is typed to return a string (but actually is a nullable param underneath). If we’re not setting that param in the attribute declaration, then it’s null and results in that TyepError. Additionally, in the middleware, $courseorid is conditionally set, only if we’re able to get this courseattributename. 

I think we want to support null in the login helper -  i.e. make get_course_attribute_name() return null or string - and then support null as a valid value for $courseorid in the middleware, so we can then pass this along to require_login() there too. It seems this was the intention of this code, as there’s already calls to require_login there - hence reporting this as a bug for now.

title: Extend the  `moodle_exception` constructor to accept the `?\Throwable $previous` and pass this to the parent
description_shown:
This is one that has bugged me for years.

The [constructor for `\Exception|https://www.php.net/manual/en/exception.construct.php]` includes a {{?Throwable $previous = null}} which allows you to chain exceptions, however we do not support it in Moodle’s exception.

I’d like to make use of this in the OAuth2 work to be able to throw a web service-releated exception (such as 404) and provide the exception which triggered it.

We can do so by adding the previous param to the {{\core\exception\moodle_exception}} constructor and providing it to the parent.

title: Course index section links still point at the old positions after a section is moved
description_shown:
Each section link in the course index points at a position rather than at a section — {{#section-3}}, {{#section-4}} and so on. Move a section and those positions change, but the course index does not update its links. They keep the numbers they were built with, so clicking them takes you to the wrong section until the page is reloaded.

The main course page does not have this problem. It renumbers its own sections as soon as one moves. Only the course index is left behind.

Steps to reproduce:

# In a course with several sections, turn editing on and open the course index.
# Drag a section in the course index to a different position.
# Without reloading, click the sections in the course index one by one.

Expected: each link takes you to the section you clicked.

Actual: the links are out by however far things moved. Reloading the page puts them right again, until the next move.

Knock-on effect worth knowing when reproducing: after landing in the wrong place, the highlighted item in the course index can be an activity from a completely different section. That part is not a separate fault — the highlight follows where the page has scrolled to, so once you have been sent to the wrong position it highlights whatever happens to be there.

Found during 5.3 QA testing, on MDLQA-22159.
